claim: Volume and Tape Gateways connect directly to AWS services through the Storage Gateway VPC endpoint, without a proxy to S3.
question: How can I use PrivateLink with Volume Gateways and Tape Gateways?

values.display: without the need for a proxy to S3

qualifiers.scope: Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway with PrivateLink

evidence.quote: Volume and Tape Gateways connect directly to AWS services through the Storage Gateway VPC endpoint without the need for a proxy to S3.

claim: To use a File Gateway on premises with PrivateLink and private virtual interfaces to reach S3 buckets, you need to set up an Amazon EC2 based proxy server, because S3 gateway endpoints are not directly accessible from on-premises environments.
question: How can I use PrivateLink with File Gateway?

values.display: Amazon EC2 based proxy server

qualifiers.scope: on-premises S3 File Gateway using PrivateLink and private VIFs
qualifiers.condition: access to S3 over a private network

evidence.quote: To use File Gateway on-premises with PrivateLink and private virtual interfaces (VIFs) to access your Amazon S3 buckets, you will need to set up an Amazon EC2 based proxy server. In order to access Amazon S3 over a private network, you need to use S3's gateway endpoints, and these endpoints are not directly accessible from on-premises environments.

claim: Volume and Tape Gateways support a SOCKS5 proxy between the on-premises gateway and AWS, and File Gateway supports an HTTP proxy.
question: Can I route my AWS Storage Gateway internet traffic through a local proxy server?

values.display: Socket Secure version 5 (SOCKS5) proxy
HyperText Transfer Protocol (HTTP) proxy

qualifiers.scope: Storage Gateway, on-premises gateway to AWS
qualifiers.condition: SOCKS5 for Volume and Tape Gateways; HTTP for File Gateway

evidence.quote: Yes. Volume and Tape Gateways support configuration of a Socket Secure version 5 (SOCKS5) proxy between your on-premises gateway and AWS. File Gateway supports configuration of a HyperText Transfer Protocol (HTTP) proxy.

claim: Volume and Tape Gateways compress data in transit and at rest, which can reduce data transfer and storage charges, and Storage Gateway uploads only data that has changed.
question: What type of data reduction does AWS Storage Gateway perform?

values.display: compression of data in-transit and at-rest

qualifiers.scope: Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway compression; changed-data upload for Storage Gateway

evidence.quote: Volume and Tape Gateways perform compression of data in-transit and at-rest which can reduce both data transfer and storage charges. The AWS Storage Gateway only uploads data that has changed, minimizing the amount of data sent over the Internet.

claim: You can throttle the network bandwidth a gateway uses to synchronize data with AWS, on a schedule, for Volume and Tape Gateways, by day of the week, time, and bandwidth rates for inbound and outbound traffic.
question: Does AWS Storage Gateway support network bandwidth throttling?

values.display: throttle network bandwidth used by the gateway

qualifiers.scope: Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway
qualifiers.condition: schedule by day of the week, time and rates

evidence.quote: Yes, you can throttle network bandwidth used by the gateway to synchronize data with AWS based on a schedule for Volume and Tape Gateways. You can specify day of the week, time, and bandwidth rates for inbound and outbound traffic.

claim: AWS Storage Gateway billing has 3 elements: storage, requests, and data transfer.
question: How will I be billed for my use of AWS Storage Gateway?

values.display: 3 elements

qualifiers.scope: AWS Storage Gateway billing

evidence.quote: There are 3 elements to how you will be billed for AWS Storage Gateway: Storage, requests, and data transfer.

claim: File Gateways store data directly in Amazon S3, and Amazon S3 bills you for the objects stored and the requests your File Gateway makes.
question: How will I be charged for file storage when using a File Gateway?

values.display: billed by Amazon S3 for the objects stored and requests

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway storage and requests

evidence.quote: File Gateways store data directly in Amazon S3. You are billed by Amazon S3 for the objects stored and requests made by your File Gateway.

claim: With File Gateway you pay for the S3 requests the gateway makes on your behalf to store and retrieve files as objects, and caching up to the capacity of your local disks can help reduce data retrieval costs.
question: When using File Gateway, will I incur S3 request charges?

values.display: pay for the S3 requests made by File Gateway

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway S3 requests

evidence.quote: You will pay for the S3 requests made by File Gateway on your behalf to store and retrieve your files in S3 as objects. The gateway caches data up to the capacity of the local disks you allocate, which can help reduce costs for data retrieval.

claim: With Storage Gateway you are billed for Internet data transfer for each GB downloaded from AWS to your gateway, and all data transfer for uploading to AWS is free.
question: How will I be charged for network data transfer to and from AWS when using AWS Storage Gateway?

values.display: All data transfer for uploading to AWS is free

qualifiers.scope: AWS Storage Gateway data transfer
qualifiers.condition: downloads from AWS to the gateway are billed; uploads to AWS are free

evidence.quote: You are billed for Internet data transfer for each GB downloaded from AWS to your gateway. All data transfer for uploading to AWS is free.

claim: For Volume and Tape Gateways you are billed only for the portion of volume or virtual tape capacity that you use, not for the provisioned size, and the fee is prorated daily.
question: How will I be charged for volume or virtual tape storage when using a volume or Tape Gateway?

values.display: only billed for the portion of volume or virtual tape capacity that you use

qualifiers.scope: Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway storage
qualifiers.condition: fee prorated daily; prices vary by region

evidence.quote: You are billed for the amount of volume and virtual tape data you store in AWS. This fee is prorated daily and prices vary by region. You are only billed for the portion of volume or virtual tape capacity that you use, not for the provisioned size of the resource.

claim: S3 does not support renaming objects, so when you rename a file or directory the S3 File Gateway copies the objects under the new keys and then deletes the originals.
question: What file system operations are supported by Amazon S3 File Gateway?

values.display: copy-put requests to create a copy of the objects in S3 under the new keys

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway rename operations

evidence.quote: Rename operations will appear atomic to your clients, but S3 does not support renaming of objects. When you rename a file or directory the gateway performs copy-put requests to create a copy of the objects in S3 under the new keys and then deletes the original objects.

claim: S3 File Gateway does not support symbolic links or hard links; trying to create a link results in an error.
question: Does Amazon S3 File Gateway support symbolic links and hard links?

values.display: Symbolic links and hard links are not supported

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway file shares

evidence.quote: Symbolic links and hard links are not supported. Attempting to create a link will result in an error.

claim: AWS recommends a single writer to the objects in an S3 bucket used by S3 File Gateway; directly overwriting an object that File Gateway wrote gives undefined behavior when read through the file share.
question: Can I have multiple writers to my S3 bucket?

values.display: We recommend a single writer to objects in your S3 bucket

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway with an S3 bucket

evidence.quote: No. We recommend a single writer to objects in your S3 bucket. If you directly overwrite or update an object previously written by File Gateway, it results in undefined behavior when the object is accessed through the file share.

claim: You can have multiple readers on a bucket managed through an S3 File Gateway; you can configure a file share as read-only and let multiple gateways read objects from the same bucket.
question: Can I have multiple gateways reading data from the same bucket?

values.display: multiple readers on a bucket

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway with an S3 bucket

evidence.quote: Yes, you can have multiple readers on a bucket managed through an Amazon S3 File Gateway. You can configure a file share as read-only, and allow multiple gateways to read objects from the same bucket.

claim: You can refresh the inventory of objects that an S3 File Gateway knows about, to see objects created by an object-based workload or another File Gateway, using the console, the file system driven cache refresh process, or the RefreshCache API.
question: Can I update my Amazon S3 File Gateway’s view of a bucket to see objects created from an object-based workload or another File Gateway?

values.display: RefreshCache API

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway

evidence.quote: Yes, you can refresh the inventory of objects that your Amazon S3 File Gateway knows about using the Console, the file system driven cache refresh process, or the RefreshCache API.

claim: The File Gateway file upload notification fires for each individual file uploaded to S3, whereas S3 event notifications include partial file uploads, so an S3 event cannot show that a file upload has completed.
question: How is a file upload notification different from an S3 event notification?

values.display: notification for each individual file that is uploaded

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway uploads

evidence.quote: The file upload notification provides a notification for each individual file that is uploaded to Amazon S3 through S3 File Gateway. S3 event notifications provide notifications that include partial file uploads so there is no way to tell from the S3 event notification that the file upload has completed.

claim: All data transferred between the S3 File Gateway and AWS storage is encrypted with SSL; by default, data stored in S3 is encrypted server-side with SSE-S3, and for each file share you can optionally use SSE-KMS.
question: What sort of encryption does Amazon S3 File Gateway use to protect my data?

values.display: Amazon S3-Managed Encryption Keys (SSE-S3)
AWS KMS-Managed Keys using SSE-KMS

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway file shares
qualifiers.condition: SSE-KMS is configured per file share

evidence.quote: All data transferred between the gateway and AWS storage is encrypted using SSL. By default, all data stored in S3 is encrypted server-side with Amazon S3-Managed Encryption Keys (SSE-S3). For each file share you can optionally configure to have your objects encrypted with AWS KMS-Managed Keys using SSE-KMS.

claim: A file share of an S3 File Gateway can be enabled for Requester Pays S3 buckets when you create it, and then you as the requester incur the charges for accessing data.
question: Can I use the gateway to access data in Requester Pays S3 buckets?

values.display: enable access to Requester Pays S3 buckets

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway file shares
qualifiers.condition: enabled when you create the file share

evidence.quote: Yes, when creating your file share you can enable access to Requester Pays S3 buckets. As a requester, you will incur the charges associated with accessing data from Requester Pays buckets.

claim: S3 File Gateway returns a large number, 8 EB, as the total capacity to applications that check storage size, because Amazon S3 does not limit total storage.
question: My application checks storage size before copying data. What storage size does the gateway return?

values.display: 8 EB

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway reported capacity

evidence.quote: The gateway returns a large number (8 EB) as your total capacity. Amazon S3 does not limit total storage.

claim: S3 File Gateway cannot write files to Amazon EFS; it stores files as objects in S3.
question: Can I use Amazon S3 File Gateway to write files to EFS?

values.display: store files as objects in S3

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway

evidence.quote: No. Amazon S3 File Gateway allows you to store files as objects in S3.

claim: Use S3 File Gateway when you want to access objects in S3 as files with standard filesystem operations; use the S3 API when your application does not need file system operations and can manage data transfer itself.
question: When should I use Amazon S3 File Gateway vs. the S3 API?

values.display: access objects in S3 as files using standard filesystem operations

qualifiers.scope: choice between S3 File Gateway and the S3 API

evidence.quote: You can use Amazon S3 File Gateway when you want to access objects in S3 as files using standard filesystem operations. Amazon S3 File Gateway additionally provides low-latency local access and efficient data transfer. You can use the S3 API when your application doesn’t require file system operations and can manage data transfer directly.
